description: A four-panel composite figure mixing one electron-backscatter-diffraction orientation map with three bright-field TEM micrographs. (a) is a colour-coded inverse pole figure (IPF) map of the solution-treated (ST) sample viewed along Z0, with a legend reading "IPF Coloring Iron FCC" and a colour triangle whose corners are 001, 101 and 111, plus a 100 µm scale bar; it shows a fully equiaxed, single-phase austenitic grain structure with no second phase visible. (b)-(d) are BF-TEM images each carrying a [001] SAED inset in which spots are labelled γ (yellow) and κ (magenta/purple). (b), 0.5 µm scale bar, green arrows mark "Intragranular κ" precipitates inside a grain. (c), 0.5 µm scale bar, orange arrows mark "Intergranular κ" precipitates at a grain boundary, with finer matrix precipitates also present. (d), 1 µm scale bar, orange arrows mark coarser, dark "Intergranular κ" precipitates decorating a grain boundary. According to the caption, (b), (c) and (d) correspond to the aged samples 550-6, 600-6 and 650-6, respectively. Apart from the scale bars, no numeric values are printed on any panel; the κ-carbide sizes (≈11, 18 and 24 nm) appear only in the citing text and are summarised in Fig. 3. Together the panels establish the fully austenitic starting state and its progressive intragranular and intergranular κ-carbide precipitation on ageing.

subfigures.description: Colour-coded IPF orientation map (EBSD) of the ST sample with legend 'IPF Coloring Iron FCC' and a 001-101-111 colour triangle; equiaxed austenite grains of many orientations, no second phase; 100 µm scale bar.
Bright-field TEM micrograph, 0.5 µm scale bar, green arrows label 'Intragranular κ' fine precipitates within an austenite grain; inset SAED along [001] with γ and κ reflections marked.
Bright-field TEM micrograph, 0.5 µm scale bar, orange arrows label 'Intergranular κ' precipitates at a grain boundary; inset SAED along [001] with γ and κ reflections marked.
Bright-field TEM micrograph, 1 µm scale bar, orange arrows label coarse dark 'Intergranular κ' precipitates along a grain boundary; inset SAED along [001] with γ and κ reflections marked.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is an IPF orientation map with a 100 µm scale bar and a legend reading 'IPF Coloring Iron FCC' with a colour triangle labelled 001, 101 and 111, showing equiaxed grains of varied orientation.
Panels (b), (c) and (d) are bright-field TEM micrographs whose scale bars read 0.5 µm, 0.5 µm and 1 µm respectively.
Each TEM panel contains an inset SAED pattern indexed to the [001] zone axis, with diffraction spots labelled γ (yellow) and κ (magenta); individual spot indices are not printed.
In (b) green arrows point to fine precipitates annotated 'Intragranular κ'; in (c) and (d) orange arrows point to precipitates annotated 'Intergranular κ' located on grain boundaries.
No numerical values are printed on any panel other than the scale bars (100 µm; 0.5 µm; 0.5 µm; 1 µm).
The caption identifies (a) as the IPF map of the ST sample and (b), (c), (d) as bright-field TEM micrographs of the aged samples 550-6, 600-6 and 650-6 respectively.
The citing text states that the IPF map reveals a fully austenitic microstructure in the ST sample.
The citing text states that the 550-6 sample shows a high density of nanoscale κ-carbides of ~11 nm with rectangular morphology uniformly precipitated within the austenite grains (Fig. 2b).

The citing text states that intragranular κ-carbides in 600-6 coarsen to ~18 nm and evolve into larger rectangular parallelepipeds forming arrays aligned along the orthogonal <100> directions of the matrix, with intergranular κ-carbide precipitation also observable (Fig. 2c).
The citing text states that aging at 650 °C coarsens intragranular κ-carbides to approximately 24 nm with more pronounced intergranular precipitation in 650-6 (Fig. 2d).

The citing text states that κ-carbide size is quantified using an equivalent-circle diameter and the evolution with aging temperature is summarised in Fig. 3, i.e. the sizes are not read from this figure.
The citing text states that the detailed κ-carbide precipitation behaviour of the Fe-30.5Mn-8Al-1C alloy during aging was reported in the authors' previous work [6].

unreadable_items: individual SAED spot indices in the (b)-(d) insets are not printed; only the γ, κ and [001] labels are readable
no numeric κ-carbide size or grain size values are printed anywhere in the figure, so the ~11/18/24 nm values cannot be verified from the pixels
the brightness/contrast of the fine intragranular precipitates in (b) is low, so individual particle outlines are only partially resolvable
